title: Smart Routing & Cascading for Global Payments
lead: Increase approval rates, reduce failed payments, and improve customer experience with automated routing logic across multiple processors.
Smart routing is a payment optimisation method that automatically chooses the best-performing processor for each transaction based on region, payment method, currency, and live performance data.
Cascading provides backup logic: when a transaction fails or times out at the first processor, it is automatically retried with alternative processors to prevent declines and recover revenue.

cards.title: Analyse and route
cards.text: Every transaction enters the routing layer, where key data points such as MID, payment type, base currency and destination currency are analysed in real time. The system then routes the payment to the processor with the highest approval probability.

cards.title: Cascade if needed
cards.text: If the first attempt declines or times out, cascading automatically reroutes the transaction to a backup processor. This helps prevent unnecessary failures caused by outages, latency or processor issues.

cards.title: Complete without disruption
cards.text: The transaction is completed seamlessly, with no visible disruption to the customer. That means fewer failed payments, lower checkout abandonment and less lost revenue.

faq.q: What is smart routing in payments?
faq.a: Smart routing selects the optimal payment processor for each transaction based on base currency, Payment type, MID, destination currency and performance data to maximise approval rates.
Cascading is a fallback mechanism that automatically retries a failed transaction with alternative processors.

faq.q: Does cascading charge a customer multiple times?
faq.a: No. The routing logic selects alternative processors for authorisation without duplicating charges.

faq.q: Why is routing important for emerging markets?
faq.a: In markets like India, LATAM, MENA, Africa, and Southeast Asia, issuer behavior and processor performance can vary a lot, so routing logic helps improve consistency.
